To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we provide theoretical guarantees for the first method that can simultaneously estimate multiple high dimensional DAG models and that this method can be used for causal inference from observational and interventional studies.

we develop a new method for learning a collection of DAG models that outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of estimation error and that this method can also be used for causal inference with interventional data.

we propose a method for joint estimation of multiple related directed Gaussian graphical models, and we prove that this method is consistent under certain regularity assumptions, and that it converges to the correct sparsity pattern faster than the method for estimating each model separately.

developing new methods to jointly estimate high dimensional DAGs from related data sources and establishing their statistical properties.

the joint estimation of DAG models can lead to faster convergence rate and improved estimation accuracy than the estimation of each DAG separately.
